articles.summary: Ranbir Kapoor reunited with his 'Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani' co-star Poorna Jagannathan at the Los Angeles premiere of 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend'.
articles.body: Ranbir Kapoor reunited with his 'Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani' co-star Poorna Jagannathan at the Los Angeles premiere of 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend'. The actress, who played Riana Sarai in the 2013 romantic drama directed by Ayan Mukerji, shared a picture with Ranbir on her social media handle, giving fans a glimpse of their reunion backstage, more than a decade after their film together.Poorna, posted the picture on Instagram, posing alongside Ranbir, who essays the role of Kabir 'Bunny' Thapar in the film. The photograph from the premiere has since caught the attention of fans, who were delighted to see the two actors together again. She also added the song 'Ilahi' sung by Mohit Chauhan, to the post.She also shared a photo from inside the theatre and posed for a photo in front of the film's poster that featured on the big screen.Poorna made headlines last year, when she got candid about facing ageism in Bollywood. The actress, who starred in Abhinay Deo's 2011 film 'Delhi Belly', said she found it difficult to get roles. "I did 'Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani' but I just felt underestimated. There was just no role for me. There was intense ageism in the industry when I was there. Things have really shifted. Priyanka, Deepika and all these people are really shifting what it means to be a woman in their forties, but not when I was there. I felt like I would've loved to have worked more, but it just didn't happen."The Los Angeles premiere of 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' took place at the David Geffen Theatre inside the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures on October 27. The special screening was attended by the film's lead cast, including Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash, along with director Nitesh Tiwari and producer Namit Malhotra. Several international celebrities, including Jada Pinkett Smith, attended the screening.Ranbir plays Lord Rama in the ambitious two-part epic, with Sai Pallavi portraying Sita and Yash taking on the villainous role of Ravana. articles.title: La vida y su dolor
articles.standfirst: Las cuatro esquinas: dolor, dolor, dolor, dolor
articles.summary: Las cuatro esquinas: dolor, dolor, dolor, dolor
articles.body: Viajo mucho en AVE. Dos veces a la semana voy a la estación de Ciudad Real. Espero los usuales retrasos desde hace unos años, quizá desde que aumentaron las compañías en la misma infraestructura, y me voy para Madrid. Unas veces son gestiones literarias o periodísticas y las más la tertulia de Telemadrid, 120 minutos, que presenta María Rey. Ayer (escribo el día del accidente) fui. Llegué a la estación de Ciudad Real y cientos de personas pululaban por aquí y allá perdidos. ¿Qué pasa?, me dije. A esta hora temprana (las 7,30) suele estar tranquila la estación. Al parecer se había suspendido el primer tren de la mañana, y ya se había trastocado todo al intentar acomodar a los pasajeros. La indignación es habitual. Si no es por una cosa (robos de cables, problemas informáticos...) es por otra. Casi siempre hay problemas. Los viajeros recordamos aquel tiempo en el que el AVE era modélico. Si se retrasaba más de cinco minutos te devolvían el 100% del dinero. Ahora si se retrasa 60 minutos el 50% y 90 el 100%. El servicio tiene un deterioro agrio que ha ido generando una rabia improductiva, una sensación de impotencia, de desgana también en muchos trabajadores. No quiero acusar, pero como usuario quiero dejar claro que la gestión es pésima. No tengo ni idea si es de Renfe o Adif. Retrasos, cambios de trenes, acumulaciones de pasajeros, angustia... En Atocha he visto gente joven sentada o tirada en el suelo. Pero nadie parece pensar en los ancianos. Son escasos los asientos. Nadie vigila que se respeten los reservados para ancianos o personas con discapacidad. Sientes que es la ley de la selva. Hay gente que trabaja en Madrid y vive en Ciudad Real y viceversa. Muchos se están planteando alternativas. Los retrasos persistentes impiden que lleguen a la hora a su trabajo. Una vez vale. Pero tantas. Hablamos mucho de cuando el AVE funcionaba bien. Era una felicidad viajar. Ahora cabreo, calor. Un amigo estuvo en un tren parado dos horas en verano sin aire acondicionado, a pleno sol, en La Mancha desértica... Estoy muy triste. Perdonadme, no puedo escribir de deporte. Solo puedo imaginar el infierno de esa gente con la que he coincidido en esa estación de Madrid que está apretada en unas obras infinitas. Las señalizaciones de los taxis son pésimas. Ves extranjeros buscándolos, desde la planta baja del primer edificio, cerca de la plaza de Atocha. Están en el otro, donde el rostro de una niña creado por Antonio López representa el paso del tiempo, la inocencia de la infancia y la esperanza frente al dolor. Allí reinó un día la muerte. Ahora vuelve por otras razones y no quiero pensar en otra cosa que en dar mi ánimo a todos los que amaban a los fallecidos.

articles.title: La tuneladora china de 135 metros de longitud: avanza a toda velocidad por el túnel ferroviario submarino de alta velocidad más largo del mundo
articles.standfirst: Trabaja 93 metros por debajo del lecho marino
articles.summary: Trabaja 93 metros por debajo del lecho marino
articles.body: Las megaestructuras requieren de megasistemas para poder ser llevadas a cabo. En este sentido, para que las redes ferroviarias puedan ser efectivas, se debe contar con tuneladoras que perforen tanto regiones montañosas como el subsuelo para que el transporte sea efectivo. Si hablamos de evolución, China puede ser uno de los países con mayor crecimiento en los últimos años y sus infraestructuras así lo corroboran. Para llevar a cabo los proyectos subterráneos, cuentan con un aparato que es de lo mejor del mundo para la creación del túnel ferroviario. Se trata de Yongzhou, una tuneladora de gran diámetro que funciona de manera autónoma por las profundidades del lecho marino. Son 135 metros de aparato que trabaja con seguridad bajo el fondo del mar, creando nuevas vías. Sus creadores consideran que el sistema inteligente es “más sensible que las personas”, de cara a detectar anomalías en el proceso de creación. “Algunos problemas son imposibles de detectar mediante la inspección humana. Uno pasa y todo parece estar bien. Un segundo después, aparece un problema. El sistema también puede recopilar los datos, identificar las condiciones relacionadas y analizar las posibles causas. Eso es de gran ayuda para la seguridad”, afirmó Dong Bing, ingeniero mecánico jefe del proyecto, el cual recibe notificaciones mandadas directamente de la tuneladora que le actualizan al segundo los procesos. Sin duda, uno de los atractivos de esta tuneladora, y de las que empieza a exportar China a todo el mundo, es que son capaces de adaptarse a diferentes terrenos y condiciones geológicas: “Podemos adaptar las máquinas a entornos subterráneos específicos, a la vez que proporcionamos soluciones integradas que combinan equipos, sistemas inteligentes y servicios técnicos durante todo el proceso de construcción”, reconoció Hao Weiqi, subdirector de la oficina del Instituto de Investigación de Tecnología de la Industria de Equipos de Alta Gama de China Railway Construction Corp en declaraciones a Global Times. Ahora, esta tuneladora se encamina a la sección más profunda del proyecto. Tras completar el 83% de la excavación, se encontrará con otra tuneladora, Dinghai, que está haciendo el proceso desde el punto opuesto. Cuando ambas se encuentren, serán desmanteladas y el túnel se habrá completado. Todo esto 93 metros debajo del lecho marino en Ningbo. Este proyecto une Ningbo y Zhoushan, con una longitud de más de 16 kilómetros de los cuales 11,21 corresponden a una sección excavada siendo el túnel ferroviario submarino más largo del mundo.

articles.body: Buckingham Palace was reportedly "blindsided" by allegations involving Meghan Markle's estranged father, former Hollywood lighting director Thomas Markle Sr. The Sun reported on Oct. 22 that Thomas Markle Jr. said he found "hundreds, if not thousands" of images depicting child sexual abuse while clearing out boxes at his father's former home in Cebu, Philippines. Markle Jr. told the newspaper that he reported the images to Philippine police and contacted the FBI in the U.S. The 82-year-old Markle denied the allegations to the Daily Mail, telling the newspaper: "I'm shocked, I'm hurt, and I'm very upset that my son is making these accusations against me. I could never do what I'm being accused of. It's the worst thing anyone could accuse me of." PRINCE HARRY MAKING 'BIG MISTAKE' THAT COULD DESTROY CHANCE OF ROYAL RECONCILIATION: EXPERT Fox News Digital reached out to Markle Sr. for comment. "Following the report, I made more than 40 phone calls to royal sources over the weekend, and nobody I spoke to had heard anything about these allegations before the story broke in The Sun," Kinsey Schofield, host of the YouTube show "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," told Fox News Digital. "My understanding is that Buckingham Palace was blindsided," she said. "They find themselves dragged into another controversy involving [the Sussexes]. And the allegations are deeply disturbing." WATCH: BUCKINGHAM PALACE WAS 'BLINDSIDED' BY THOMAS MARKLE SR. ALLEGATIONS: EXPERT Fox News Digital reached out to Buckingham Palace for comment. In 2018, a letter was sent to the Metropolitan Police and Royalty and Specialist Protection. That letter was subsequently shared with me. It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father, and I was given assurances that these were being investigated." "I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications' distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them," she wrote. "I trusted that the authorities were doing the same for other families. "Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children." WATCH: KING CHARLES MAY PRIVATELY SUPPORT MEGHAN MARKLE AMID CONTROVERSY: EXPERT The Metropolitan Police said its records show that the letter was received in January 2019, not 2018. Meghan's spokesperson subsequently acknowledged the discrepancy, saying the police's timestamped records should be treated as authoritative. The letter was written by Markle Sr.'s first wife, Roslyn Markle, also known as Roslyn Loveless, ITV News reported on Oct. 26. The outlet said it had reviewed the letter, which contained allegations of sexual abuse against Markle Sr. He has denied the allegations. Melvin Matibag, director of the Philippines' National Bureau of Investigation, told The Associated Press that the FBI had requested the bureau's assistance in investigating Markle Jr.'s allegations against his father. Philippine Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla separately told the AP that the Philippine National Police was also investigating Markle Jr.'s allegations against his father. Remulla did not elaborate. A spokesperson for Remulla told Fox News Digital that the Philippine National Police (PNP) is continuing its investigation. Schofield said the royal family would likely keep its distance from the Sussexes as its members prioritize their duties while the investigation continues. But Harry has repeatedly shared private conversations through interviews, documentaries and his memoir. The king would be reluctant to have a sensitive conversation on this topic with Prince Harry without reassurance that it would remain private." articles.title: Angel Studios draws line in sand with Hollywood, bans sex scenes, profanity in bold new pledge
articles.summary: Angel Studios bans nudity, on-screen sex and certain profanity in a sweeping new policy while giving 3 million Angel Guild members veto power.
articles.body: FIRST ON FOX — Angel Studios is drawing a line in the sand against Hollywood's approach to entertainment, announcing sweeping new content standards that ban on-screen sex, nudity and certain profanity while promising millions of paying members the power to decide which movies and television shows make the cut. In an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital, Angel Studios co-founder and Chief Content Officer Jeff Harmon said the entertainment industry has increasingly lost touch with the families it once served, prompting his company to establish what it calls "The Angel Promise." "I think Hollywood generally kind of lives in a bubble," Harmon said. "These are excellent craftsmen. They're the best storytellers in the world. Hollywood has built the best storytelling infrastructure in the world." COMEDIAN LEANNE MORGAN CALLS OUT HOLLYWOOD FOR LIVING IN A 'BUBBLE' AND MISJUDGING WHAT AUDIENCES WANT TO SEE "But at the same time, they've kind of drifted more and more away from the values-based audience that they used to serve," Harmon said. "And with that, in our view, as brothers and as fathers, as a father, Hollywood hasn't been giving me consistently what I need. Once in a while, you get a good one, but you have to sift through all these things to find your good movies and your good stories." The new initiative, announced Thursday, establishes three core commitments governing Angel's entertainment offerings, namely, audience approval of content, strict standards involving sex and language, and expanded parental controls. "We promise there's never going to be nudity, and there'll never be sex on screen," Harmon said, explaining that families participating in the Angel Guild will not have to worry about encountering such material when evaluating potential projects. The company is also drawing a firm boundary around profanity, pledging that Angel's original productions will not misuse God's name. NEW STUDY REVEALS THE SINGLE MOST CRITICAL FACTOR IN WHETHER CHILDREN KEEP THEIR FAITH INTO ADULTHOOD "This is a completely unique one," Harmon said. "This has never really happened in Hollywood history." Harmon described the restriction as part of the company's effort to build trust with religious families. "What we promise our viewers is that this timeless principle that's thousands of years old, and we're a very faith-friendly studio, is that we're not going to have misuse of God's name on the system on any Angel original content," Harmon said. "So any content we create. Where we are originating, meaning it comes to Angel first, those shows, those TV shows and movies, will not have misuse of God's name, so that families of faith, 'cause we're a faith-friendly studio, can trust that language won't be there." Under the new standards, the company also prohibits use of the F-word in its stories and profanity in titles submitted for children ages 12 and younger. HOLLYWOOD PRODUCER BEHIND 'APOLLO 13' REJECTS POLITICS IN HIS MOVIES, SEEKS TO UNITE AUDIENCES The announcement represents a significant effort to distinguish Angel from traditional Hollywood studios, with the company placing its audience at the center of decisions about what gets produced and distributed. Harmon said the Angel Guild, which has approximately 3 million paying members, gives viewers an opportunity to approve or reject projects before they enter the company's entertainment ecosystem. "This is the first time in history that a major Hollywood studio, or top 10 studio in the United States, has come and said, we're going to let the audience have a veto right," Harmon said. Under Angel's stated policy, films and television series must receive a score of at least 70 out of 100 from Guild members to qualify for inclusion in its entertainment ecosystem. Harmon said the founders' experiences raising children helped shape the new standards. "Angel was co-founded by four brothers and a cousin," he said, adding that the founders have 34 children between them. CREATING THE DEFINITIVE MOUNT RUSHMORE OF PIXAR MOVIES FROM A PARENTS' VIEWING PERSPECTIVE The goal, he explained, was to create entertainment that parents could trust without having to sift through potentially objectionable content. The third component of the Angel Promise focuses on parental controls. Angel says Guild members will help establish recommended age ratings and plain-language descriptions of potentially sensitive material, while new controls in the Angel app will allow parents to tailor viewing choices to their families. Harmon said the broader ambition is to reshape the relationship between filmmakers and audiences. "Our goal was to set out and try to fix this problem of kind of stepping out of the Hollywood bubble and stepping into middle America's shoes," he said. The company says its Guild has paid out nearly $300 million to filmmakers, while Harmon said more than 100 films were available for members to vote on at the time of the interview. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP For Harmon, the new promise is about establishing permanent standards that will outlast any individual film, filmmaker or executive, and give families greater influence over the entertainment they consume. Some of the studio's prominent recent films include "David" and "The King of Kings."

articles.summary: Explore Ethan Hawke's profound insights on life, creativity, and the importance of detaching from ego and envy. Discover how genuine passion can lead to artistic fulfillment and joy.
articles.body: Ethan Hawke is well known for his philosophical take on life and has spent years in the entertainment industry. From becoming a rom-com heartthrob in his youth in the industry to becoming a seasoned star in Hollywood. Today’s quote of the day is about understanding that sometimes things can be done without joining the rat race, and rather than focusing on your ego and the superficial things in life, you can get more out of life by simply enjoying things without letting your ego get the best of you.The quote from Ethan Hawke reads, "If you can channel the best part of you that is bigger than yourself, where it’s not about your ego and not about getting ahead, then you can have fun and you aren’t jealous of others. You see other people's talent as another branch of your own. You can keep it rooted in joy. Life is long, and there are plenty of opportunities to make mistakes. The point of it all is to learn.”What does the quote by Ethan Hawke mean?Ethan Hawke shared today’s quote of the day during an extensive Q&A interview that he had with Stephen Galloway for The Hollywood Reporter series ‘The Hollywood Masters,’ which was published on February 8, 2015.Ethan Hawke’s quote for today explores one of the greatest obstacles in any creative, professional, or personal life: the friction between your ego and the authentic purpose that you are aiming for. At its core, the quote serves as a philosophy for how to sustain long-term artistic fulfillment, avoid burnout, and cultivate a mind free from envy.Taking his career and experience into account, Hawke talks about moments in life where when you approach your work or passion primarily to gain status, fame, or financial success or to simply get ahead, your worth and aim can entirely get dependent on external validation. This makes failure feel much worse and catastrophic, while success feels small and fleeting. However, if you can focus on the craft, the story, or the contribution itself rather than personal glory, you can detach your identity from outcomes. You move from performing for approval to participating in something meaningful.Other than that, jealousy is another common emotion in life; however, once you move past the emotion, you simply look towards people as a branch rather than a competitor all the time. You will also be able to enjoy life and the things that you do more freely. By completely stripping away your ego and jealousy, you can reclaim the playfulness of creating things for the simple happiness of doing so rather than comparing yourself to other people.The core takeaway from Hawke’s insightful words is about understanding and advocating for a shift from an ego-driven life to a more relaxed life. When you treat art, work, and personal growth as a lifelong practice of learning rather than a race, you unlock lasting freedom, creativity, and inner peace.About Ethan Hawke’s early lifeEthan Hawke was born on November 6, 1970, in Austin, Texas. From an early age, he led a simple life, which was heavily influenced by his parents. His parents, Leslie (née Green) and James Hawke, were high school sweethearts who married young while they were studying together at the University of Texas in Austin. His father was an actuarial student, and his mother was a charity worker.When Hawke was only three years old, his parents divorced in 1974, following which Hawke was raised primarily by his mother. He moved around a lot with his mother and lived in places like Atlanta, Georgia, and New York City before he eventually settled down in New Jersey when his mother remarried. As for his schooling, Hawke attended West Windsor-Plainsboro High School South in New Jersey, though he later transferred to the Hun School of Princeton, a private college preparatory school, from where he graduated in 1988.Ethan Hawke’s rise to fameThe beloved star’s love for acting and theater started from an early age, when at age 13, he started acting classes at the McCarter Theatre on the Princeton campus. He later made his stage debut in a school production of George Bernard Shaw's ‘Saint Joan.’ His feature debut came a year later. At age 14, Hawke starred alongside River Phoenix in the sci-fi adventure film 'Explorers,' which helped him officially enter the acting industry.He took a break from acting to study at Carnegie Mellon University's Drama Department. He dropped out after being cast as Todd Anderson in Peter Weir’s ‘Dead Poets Society’ alongside Robin Williams, which was a big commercial success. Hawke was 18 years old at the time.Since then, he has been a consistent name in the Hollywood industry, and some of his most popular projects over the years include ‘The Before Trilogy’ (1995 to 2013), ‘First Reformed’ (2017), ‘Boyhood’ (2014), ‘Training Day’ (2001), ‘Predestination’ (2014), ‘Before the Devil Knows You're Dead’ (2007), ‘The Black Phone’ (2021), ‘Reality Bites’ (1994), and many others.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Sara Ali Khan in trouble for visiting Kedarnath temple, Islamic cleric issues 'fatwa', calls it 'impermissible and haram' under Sharia
articles.summary: Sara Ali Khan is often seen expressing her love for Kedarnath and also visits the temple at regular intervals.
articles.body: Sara Ali Khan is often seen expressing her love for Kedarnath and also visits the temple at regular intervals. This time around, her visit has come under scrunity as Uttar Pradesh-based Islamic cleric Maulana Mufti Shahabuddin Razvi Barelvi has issued a fatwa over the actress offering prayers at the Hindu shrineThe controversy follows after Sara’s visit on Sunday, October 25, when she was spotted standing in a queue for darshan. After offering prayers, the actor was seen outside the temple with her hands folded.In a video statement, the Islamic cleric said that worshipping according to another religion was “impermissible and haram under Sharia”. He also called on Sara to seek forgiveness from Allah, urging her to repent “like a guilty person”.“Several youngsters have asked me whether Sara’s act of worshipping at Kedarnath is permissible under Sharia. I want to make it clear that such acts are not permissible,” the cleric said in the video.This is not the first time Sara has faced criticism from religious figures over her visits to Kedarnath. A fatwa is a religious opinion or ruling on a question of Islamic law issued by a qualified Islamic scholar.Sara, daughter of actors Amrita Singh and Saif Ali Khan, has been visiting Kedarnath regularly for the past four years. Her acting debut, ‘Kedarnath’, which also starred the late Sushant Singh Rajput, had faced opposition from right-wing groups in Uttarakhand ahead of its release in 2018.Meanwhile, the Badrinath-Kedarnath Temple Committee (BKTC), which oversees the management of both shrines, has made it mandatory for non-Hindu visitors wishing to offer prayers at the temples to submit an affidavit.BKTC Chief Executive Officer Sohan Singh Rangar confirmed to News18 that Sara’s team had submitted the required affidavit before her visit.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: In 2017, four artists bought Nina Simone’s childhood home for $95,000 to save it from demolition; Inside the restoration of the music legend’s historic 650-square-foot house in North Carolina
articles.summary: In a quiet corner of Tryon, North Carolina, a small white clapboard house once held the beginnings of a voice that would change music and challenge a
articles.body: In a quiet corner of Tryon, North Carolina, a small white clapboard house once held the beginnings of a voice that would change music and challenge a nation. From 1933 to 1937, Eunice Kathleen Waymon, later known as Nina Simone lived in the three-room, 650-square-foot home nestled in the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains according to Architectural Digest. It was here that her extraordinary gift at the piano first appeared. For decades the house was largely forgotten, falling into disrepair and facing possible demolition. Today, after a careful rescue by four artists and a full restoration with the National Trust for Historic Preservation, the modest structure stands again as a living piece of Black cultural memory, with plans to welcome visitors in the years ahead.Nina Simone’s home in a reimagined versionIn late 2016, painter Adam Pendleton learned the house was for sale. A friend who owned property nearby reached out, hoping someone would step in before it was lost. Pendleton thought of a line from June Jordan’s 1978 “Poem for South African Women”: “We are the ones we have been waiting for.” He later recalled, “I realized that the someone to spring into action, the someone to do something, was me.” He contacted fellow artist Rashid Johnson, who shared his deep respect for Simone as both musician and thinker. Together they invited Julie Mehretu and Ellen Gallagher to join them. As Architectural Digest revealed, in 2017 the four artists purchased the house for $95,000, choosing to act as a collective rather than as individual buyers.Why artists stepped forward for Nina Simone’s homeThe decision was focused on creating a meaning. By pooling their names and networks, they wanted to show that protecting Simone’s early home was a shared cultural duty. Rashid Johnson put it simply: “We all reconciled our enthusiasm and recognition of how these kinds of sites; these kinds of opportunities, provide things that sometimes are hard to articulate. Sometimes it’s just the feeling of being in a place that matters, and that tells the story of someone that matters.” They then partnered with the African American Cultural Heritage Action Fund, part of the National Trust for Historic Preservation, which took the lead on the long-term care of the property.Careful hands to restore Nina Simone’s placeThe restoration kept as much of the original fabric as possible. Stamped tin roof shingles were carefully replicated. Remnants of old linoleum stayed in place. Original pine walls and wood floors were refinished. The porch ceiling was painted haint blue, a hue believed to ward off evil spirits, with roots in the traditions of the Gullah Geechee people, descendants of enslaved Africans in the American South. Modern needs were met quietly with geothermal heating, fire-suppression systems, and an ADA-compliant ramp. Outside, a swept dirt yard was recreated in the African tradition once common in the rural South. Archaeologists found the foundation of an old work shed and marked it for visitors. At the back of the property stands a nearly century-old magnolia tree, nicknamed “Sweetie Mae,” that was already growing when Simone was a child.A place meant to lastBrent Leggs, the Action Fund’s executive director and strategic advisor to the CEO of the National Trust described the goal clearly to Architectural Digest: “Our role was to ensure the home wasn’t just preserved, but protected forever as a living symbol of Nina Simone’s life. And our vision was to create a singular place where her legacy will endure.” Pendleton still remembers his first visit. Standing on the porch and looking toward the church where Simone once played, he felt the weight of the moment. “That overwhelmed me, this idea that everything begins somewhere,” he said. “And this is where it began for her.” In Tryon, the childhood home of Nina Simone has been given a second life, not as a museum frozen in time, but as a living space where her story continues to be felt.Who was Nina Simone?Nina Simone was a singular American musician, singer, and civil rights activist whose voice carried both beauty and fire. Born Eunice Kathleen Waymon in Tryon, North Carolina, in 1933, she trained as a classical pianist before moving to jazz, blues and protest songs that spoke directly to the struggles of her time. Her songs “Mississippi Goddam” and “To Be Young, Gifted and Black” made her a power to be reckoned with in the fight for equality. For much of her later life she lived abroad, but her music and indomitable spirit continue to connect with people decades after her death in 2003.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Josh Duhamel urges voters to save ‘God’s country’ ahead of midterms
articles.summary: Actor Josh Duhamel shared an Instagram video urging Minnesota voters to hit the polls for midterm elections, calling the state "worth saving."
articles.body: Josh Duhamel is encouraging Minnesotans to get out and vote in a new video he shared on Instagram. The actor took to social media to send out a "PSA to the great people of Minnesota," rallying residents to pack the polls in what he dubbed "God's country." "I just wanted to take a second to remind you that the midterms are coming up. This is such an important, such an important time. We have to get out there. We have to vote. Every single person," he said. "Minnesota is my second favorite state in the whole country, right behind North Dakota, but I absolutely love it there. It is God's country. It is worth saving. It is absolutely worth saving." While he said he "would never tell you who to vote for," he believes voting is one's "job as an American citizen" and a "sacred duty." JOSH DUHAMEL SAYS HIS HEART RATE DROPS 25% AT OFF-GRID MINNESOTA CABIN "And it is a blessing that we get to get out there and pick who makes decisions for us," he added. "So please, everybody, let's get 100 percent turnout. Everybody, please, vote in this year's midterms. Go Viks! Woo!" In the caption, Duhamel encouraged his followers to "Bring a group to the voting booths on Nov 3" and to share the post "with everyone you know!!" Although the actor didn't endorse any candidates, people in the comments section made their own assumptions as to what he meant when he said the state is "worth saving." "Worth saving means vote red. Good man @joshduhamel," one fan wrote in the comments section. "Red red red all down the ballot," another added, while a third wrote, "Vote RED! Save America." Others went the other way, with one writing, "Vote blue save us all!!!! 💙💙💙💙💙." Another said, "Let’s go blue! Please save our children! 💙" The "Ransom Canyon" star listed his home in Los Angeles in July, a little over a year after he and his family moved from California to Fargo, North Dakota. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE In addition to his home in North Dakota, Duhamel also has a residence about an hour and a half away in Minnesota, where he likes to go in order to spend "time off the grid." "I learned that I'd spent too much time sort of luxuriating in the amenities of the modern world and getting out there and having to learn how to do some of the basics that I hadn't done for so long was really, really good," he told People in September 2025. I'm constantly doing something, fixing something, working on something, taking care of the family, pulling the kids on a tube, cooking, all these things that are just basics that we take for granted." The actor lives in the cabin with his wife, Audra Mari, and their 2-year-old son, Shepherd. Duhamel's 13-year-old son Axl, whom he shares with his ex-wife Fergie, also spends time at the home. He said his older son is "not on his iPad" all day but rather playing sports, exploring the woods and overall enjoying the outdoors. "And then I have a little baby who's going to experience the same thing. Someday, I hope to pass this on to them [so] they're able to share it with their kids. It's really important to me that they have this. It's not just about having all the amenities and all the luxuries that we become so used to. It's really about family. It's about legacy," he said. articles.title: Quote of the day by BTS’ RM: ‘Happiness is not something that you have to achieve, If you change your perspective a little bit, this moment could be the most beautiful moment of our lives'
articles.summary: Discover BTS leader RM's powerful quote on happiness, emphasizing the importance of changing perspectives to find joy in the journey. Learn about his philosophy and early life influences in this insightful article.
articles.body: In an era driven by constant hustle and moving goals, BTS’s RM talked about a timely reality check on how we measure peace of mind. Today’s quote from the beloved musician is all about understanding and directly challenging the belief that happiness requires a final stamp of achievement. Instead, he highlighted the power of reframing our current circumstances and changing the perspective of how we live life.The quote of the day from the BTS leader reads, "Happiness is not something that you have to achieve. You can still be happy during the process of achieving something. So if you change your perspective a little bit, I know many people are going through tough times right now, but this moment could be the most beautiful moment of our lives.”What does the quote mean?Today’s quote from RM, whose real name is Kim Namjoon, is from his speech during the BTS 2015 ‘HYYH (The Most Beautiful Moment in Life) On Stage’ concert series, which was held from November 27–29, 2015, at the SK Olympic Handball Gymnasium in Seoul, South Korea.RM’s quote directly talks about how modern society views success, self-worth, and emotional fulfillment. His speech is about our changing our perspective and taking a different approach to living in the present rather than postponing happiness for a future milestone. While most people view happiness as something that can only be awarded at the end of a long journey. The situation can be different; after graduating, securing a promotion, or achieving financial stability, however, the motive stays the same. RM points out that treated this way, happiness becomes a target rather than something that you feel and enjoy in the moment. When one goal is reached, another takes its place, keeping true fulfillment perpetually out of reach.Youth and personal growth are mostly full of uncertainty, failure, and self-doubt. Along with that, society also often frames these difficult phases as obstacles that delay happiness. RM argues that the process of working through hardship is itself meaningful because the resilience and knowledge gained while striving for a goal contributes directly to personal character. Experiencing solidarity, effort, and growth during tough times holds intrinsic beauty, regardless of the final result.By sharing this insight, RM offered a comforting reminder to people about how you do not need to wait until you "make it" to deserve peace, joy, and self-acceptance.About RM’s early lifeKim Namjoon (RM) was born on September 12, 1994, in Dongjak-gu, Seoul, South Korea, and spent his childhood in the Ilsan District of Goyang, where his family relocated when he was around four years old. From a young age, RM was heavily involved in his studies and was an exceptionally bright student, scoring in the top 1% nationally on South Korea’s university entrance examinations and holding an IQ of 148. While his parents initially wanted him to pursue a traditional academic career because of his high grades, his interest lay more in the music industry.He also taught himself how to speak English fluently by regularly watching the American sitcom ‘Friends’ with his mother, as well as spending four months studying abroad in New Zealand when he was 12 years old. His interest in music sparked around the same time he heard the song ‘Fly’ by Epik High. Inspired by the legendary group and later American artists like Eminem, he realized his poetry could be turned into song lyrics and began writing rap tracks.He started as an underground rapper from 2007 to 2009 and started posting tracks and covers online. His career with BTS started in 2010 when he signed with Big Hit Entertainment. Later, on June 13, 2013, he debuted as the leader and main rapper of BTS under the stage name Rap Monster. Around 2015, the group started gaining traction after the release of their album, ‘The Most Beautiful Moment in Life.' In November 2017, he officially changed his stage name to RM, which stands for "Real Me."To date, RM and BTS continue to rise to global dominance, and earlier this year, they released their first album in around 3 to 4 years, titled 'ARIRANG.'Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Elke Sommer, star of Pink Panther film ‘A Shot in the Dark’ and ‘The Prize,’ dies at 85
articles.summary: Elke Sommer, the striking blonde bombshell of German descent who was a mainstay of 1960s Hollywood movies including “The Prize” and “A Shot in the Dark,” has died.
articles.body: Elke Sommer, the striking blonde bombshell of German descent who was a mainstay of 1960s Hollywood comedies and espionage movies including “The Prize” and “A Shot in the Dark,” has died. She was 85. Sommer died at home in Bel Air, in Los Angeles, on Wednesday, her stepson Sebastian Walther told the German outlet Bild. The Los Angeles Police Department told The Associated Press that it responded to the death of an 85-year-old woman on Sommer’s block Wednesday night. With big almond eyes and golden locks, often styled high in a beehive, Sommer worked with some of the biggest stars of the time, including Paul Newman in “The Prize,” Peter Sellers in the Pink Panther film “A Shot in the Dark,” James Garner and Dick Van Dyke in “The Art of Love,” Bob Hope in “Boy, Did I Get a Wrong Number!” and Dean Martin and Sharon Tate in “The Wrecking Crew.” Sommer was born Elke Schletz in Berlin in the midst of the World War II, on Nov. 5, 1940, though the family had to evacuate to the south in 1942. Her father, who died when she was 14, was a Protestant pastor. She’d intended to study languages, but during a trip to Italy with her mother, Renata, in 1958, she caught the eye of someone in the Italian film industry who invited her to appear in her first film: “The Friend of the Jaguar.” Actor and filmmaker Vittorio De Sica noticed her too, and soon she was working nonstop throughout Europe, in Italy, Spain and England, with the newly adopted surname Sommer. Her big Hollywood break came from producer Pandro S. Berman, who had seen her in a German drama that screened for the Golden Globes, and offered her a role in “The Prize” where she played chaperone and love interest to Newman’s Nobel Prize-winning character. In the trade publication Variety’s review, they wrote that Sommer, “hasn’t a very scintillating role, but has the looks to make that a secondary issue.” And it would win her the Golden Globe for most promising newcomer. In Blake Edwards’ Pink Panther sequel “A Shot in the Dark,” she played Maria Gambrelli, a maid framed for murder, who also sparks the romantic interest of Sellers’ Inspector Clouseau. She also posed for Playboy Magazine around that time, in photographs shot by her first husband Joe Hyams. They married in November 1964 and divorced in 1981. In 1993 she married German hotelier Wolf Walther, who died in July at age 77. Sommer didn’t take the sex symbol designation too seriously, saying that it was essentially meaningless. She told Film Talk in a 2014 interview that some of her favorite actors, like Rita Hayworth and Ava Gardner, were also considered sex symbols. Besides, she said, she was always just acting the part. “My whole life, I have been directed, I have been produced, I spoke the lines written for the character,” she said in the interview. “I was always playing, and the only thing I could bring was my energy. So what is it, this sex appeal? Why was I voted in this list of most sexy women? It’s not because of my looks or anything; it’s because of the energy.”
